sentences.text: Based on its fossil bone, Laornis is thought to have been a semi-aquatic bird with a body size at least that of a large goose.
If Laornis was a wading bird, it likely stood about one meter (3 to 4 feet) tall.
The name Laornis translates to "stone bird" derived from Ancient Greek words for stone and bird.
The species name edvardsianus honors the French paleontologist Alphonse Milne-Edwards for his work on fossil birds.
Fossils of Laornis were found in the Hornerstown Formation in Pemberton Township, New Jersey, United States.
Laornis has been variously allied with the orders Charadriiformes and Gruiformes and is tentatively placed in its own family, Laornithidae.
Laornis might have belonged to the extinct family of stilt-legged waterfowl known as Presbyornithidae.
It is possible that Laornis was an ancient pseudotooth bird, a group of seabirds with unclear affiliations.
The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Laornis as Graculavidae.
The Paleobiology Database classifies Laornis within the family Graculavidae.
The sediments containing Laornis fossils were deposited approximately 66 to 63 million years ago.
The Paleobiology Database records the time range of Laornis as the Maastrichtian stage, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
